source_name: LinkPlus IT — Kosovo software house
why_relevant: Prishtina/Skopje custom software firm active in the Kosovo banking-tech ecosystem (co-organiser with ProCredit Bank Kosova of DevCon Prishtina). Sponsorship/partnership visibility is a weak but real signal of commercial relationships with banks; its portfolio pages may name bank clients.

source_name: Horizon Plus — case study: modernizing the Central Bank of Kosovo's digital platform
why_relevant: Concrete example of the cell's core hypothesis: a supplier publishes a named Kosovo financial-sector engagement (BQK digital platform) as a case study. The site's case-studies index is worth monitoring as a standing source, and the item itself points at a BQK contract to hunt in procurement records.

source_name: Printec Group — news / success stories (regional ATM, cash-automation, POS integrator)
why_relevant: Printec is a major SEE banking-technology integrator (ATM/cash automation/self-service) and has a registered Kosovo entity (PRINTEC L.L.C., Prishtina, per D&B). Its newsroom/success-story pages are a canonical place for Kosovo bank deployment announcements.

source_name: NCR Atleos — newsroom / customer stories
why_relevant: One of the two global ATM/self-service OEMs supplying Balkan banks (directly or via integrators). Vendor newsroom and customer stories are where an ATM fleet refresh or ATM-as-a-Service deal with a Kosovo bank would be disclosed if it is disclosed anywhere.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — news / case studies
why_relevant: The other global ATM/branch-automation OEM with strong SEE presence; announces bank-named ATM/recycler/branch-transformation deals and managed-services contracts that buyers in Kosovo would not publish.

source_name: Temenos — customer stories / press releases
why_relevant: Leading core-banking vendor that publishes named client wins and go-lives; any Kosovo bank core replacement on Temenos Transact/T24 would most plausibly surface first as a Temenos press release or customer story rather than in a Kosovo award notice.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld — customer technographics profiles for Kosovo banks
why_relevant: Aggregator that maps named institutions to the software vendors they buy from. Profiles exist for Raiffeisen Bank Kosova and ProCredit Bank Kosovo, so it acts as a pointer telling you which vendor's newsroom/reference pages to go hunt for the underlying contract.

source_name: App store developer/package metadata for Kosovo bank apps (Google Play / Apple App Store)
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: the Android package id and listed developer expose which vendor actually built a Kosovo bank's digital channel (e.g. ProCredit Kosovo's app under com.quipugmbh.*), naming a supplier relationship no procurement notice discloses. Cheap, structured, and updated on every release.

source_name: ATM Marketplace / Kiosk Marketplace vendor directories and news
why_relevant: Trade-press vendor directory plus news covering ATM/self-service deployments and deals. Serves both as an actor map for the ATM supply side and as a place where smaller regional deployment wins (incl. Balkans) are reported when vendors push them out.

source_name: SeeNews — SEE business wire (IT/banking contract coverage)
why_relevant: Regional business newswire that reports vendor contract wins in SEE banking (e.g. Asseco SEE ATM network renewal in Serbia). Acts as a secondary catch for Kosovo vendor announcements that never reach a global newsroom.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet Kosovo company profiles (vendor local entities)
why_relevant: Confirms which international banking-technology vendors have registered Kosovo entities (PRINTEC L.L.C. Prishtinë, ASSECO SEE SH.P.K.), giving exact legal names to match against procurement award notices and business-registry filings — the bridge between the supply-side and the tender-side workstream.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association (SHBK / Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës)
why_relevant: Not a vendor source itself, but its events, conferences and sponsor lists routinely expose which technology suppliers court and serve Kosovo banks — a reliable local-language pointer into the supply-side actor map and often the first public place a vendor-bank relationship is visible.

source_name: Integrity Watch Kosovo (Kosova Democratic Institute / TI Kosova)
why_relevant: Open-data platform joining public procurement (winning companies, contract values, procedure types) with asset declarations and political finance, with automated conflict-of-interest 'red flags'. Explicitly offers CSV, XLS and JSON downloads for procurement data and states it uses the PPRC procurement API. Trilingual manuals (en/sq/sr). Useful both as a dataset and as a pointer to the PPRC API and to buyer/vendor taxonomies.

source_name: Balkan Tender Watch (regional CSO coalition)
why_relevant: Regional anti-corruption coalition (since 2012; members include Kosovo Foundation for Open Society, Open Society Serbia, OSF BiH, CCC North Macedonia) that publishes shadow reports on Kosovo public procurement, benchmarking tools and monitoring manuals. Its documents name the local monitoring NGOs, portals and recurring problem categories — a directory of where further Kosovo procurement sources live.

source_name: RKS Open Data portal — PPRC/KRPP datasets (tenderat, prokurimi elektronik)
why_relevant: Kosovo's national CKAN-style open-data portal carries PPRC datasets tagged 'tenderat' and 'prokurimi elektronik' in XLSX and other formats — a second, often more analyst-friendly distribution channel than the OCDS API, and one that also reveals what other institutions publish procurement-adjacent data.

source_name: NjoftimePublike.com — daily tender notice aggregation (Kosovo/Albania)
why_relevant: Low-cost Albanian-language service that aggregates daily tender notices from institutions and media across Kosovo and Albania and delivers them to subscribers. Media-sourced notices are valuable because some Kosovo notices (and private-sector RFPs) appear in press before or instead of the portal.

source_name: eKapija Tenderi — regional Western Balkans tender aggregator
why_relevant: Serbian-language commercial aggregator claiming to process 350+ tender sources daily across the region (BiH, Serbia, Montenegro) using CPV classification. Even where Kosovo coverage is thin, its source list and CPV-based taxonomy is a pointer to which portals and publication channels exist in the Western Balkans, useful for regional benchmarking of banking/payments procurement.

source_name: GlobalTenders — Kosovo tenders
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that states it harvests Kosovo's official authority and agency websites and organises notices into searchable categories. Its category tree is a useful hint at which Kosovo buyers publish outside the central portal.

source_name: TenderImpulse — Kosovo tenders with dated archive and email alerts
source_subtype: commercial tender aggregator with dated archive
why_relevant: Aggregator that states it draws from e-procurement portals, government sites, newspapers, multilateral organisations and NGOs, and exposes date-addressable archive pages (per-day Kosovo tender lists). The dated archive structure is what makes it valuable: it preserves notices after they expire from the official portal.

source_name: TendersOnTime — global procurement intelligence, Kosovo and EBRD coverage
source_subtype: global commercial tender aggregator (incl. IFI notices)
why_relevant: Aggregator that indexes not only country notices but also IFI streams (dedicated EBRD notices page, Europe/EuropeAid pages) and covers contract awards and procurement plans, not just live notices. Procurement plans are the earliest signal available for a banking/payments pipeline.

source_name: WBIF Procurements — Western Balkans Investment Framework tenders & opportunities
why_relevant: Aggregated listing of upcoming and current procurement opportunities tied to WBIF-financed investments across the Western Balkans including Kosovo. Donor-financed contracts (digital infrastructure, financial-sector TA) are procured outside the national portal, so this is a channel the OCDS feed structurally misses.

source_name: Lëvizja FOL — public procurement monitoring reports (Kosovo)
why_relevant: The NGO behind Prokurimi i Hapur; publishes Albanian-language procurement monitoring reports (e.g. 'Monitorimi i Prokurimit Publik në Kosovë') whose methodology sections enumerate data sources, buyer categories and recurring irregularities. Useful for local terminology and for identifying which contracting authorities repeatedly procure IT/financial services.

source_name: BIRN Kosova / Gazeta Jeta ne Kosove
why_relevant: The long-form investigative arm behind KALLXO; produces multi-month procurement investigations and data-driven pieces including analyses built on commercial banks' public auction notices (foreclosure sales), which is a rare banking-sector data trail.
